reading.body:
Apple's Prineville campus in Crook County, Oregon is a multi-building facility announced in 2012 on roughly 160 acres, but the operator publishes no power capacity figure for the site. The campus appears in this registry as four separate rows with generic labels and no distinguishing building identifiers, reflecting the absence of citable street addresses for individual buildings within the campus despite verification of the overall campus location.

Among Oregon's 133 mapped data center facilities, only eight operators publish power capacity figures in their specifications, totaling 156.6 MW of disclosed IT load. This campus does not rank within that published cohort because Apple has not disclosed its Prineville power draw, placing it outside the measurable capacity picture for the state despite its size and announced scale.

Without published specifications, this campus cannot be assessed as a determinant of AI scaling in the region. The lack of disclosed capacity, combined with the absence of facility-level addressing within the campus, means this site does not contribute a quantifiable figure to the grid constraint analysis that determines which data center deployments matter to AI infrastructure planning.
